analysis.title: CTA Update
key_insights: CTAs held their positions through the volatility after the US midterm election and the US CPI report. They remain short to 'max short' in US equities and US Treasuries and 'max long' USD across all FX pairs Citi tracks.

US equities: buy signals for CTAs are within 1% of current levels. Funds flip back long SPX above 7676 (+0.8% vs 7612) and begin covering NDX shorts above 28632 (+0.9% vs 28374 NQZ6). RTY is 'max short' with its first cover level at 2855, +0.1% vs 2855.
SPX: CTAs were briefly signaled to add to shorts on last week's selloff. That was put on hold when the market rebounded into moderately short territory this week.
Europe equities: CTAs flipped long and are adding to longs as SX5E rebounded. Buying halts if SX5E reverses below 6313 (VGZ6 ref 6377).
EM and Japan equities: CTAs are 'max short' despite the rebound. Cover levels are further away than for US indices, at 1654 in MXEF (+4.3% vs 1586 MESZ6) and 62623 in NKY (+1.9% vs 61440 NKZ6).

US rates: after the post-CPI selloff, CTAs went back to 'max short' in TU, FV and TY. They still have room to add shorts in US below 106-23 (USZ6 ref 107-01) and in WN below 108-03 (WNZ6 ref 108-16). The signal to start buying again is 106-11 in TY (TYZ6 ref 106-03).

European rates: CTAs are moderately short duration outside OATs, where they are 'max short'. Flip-to-long signals in Bunds (123.28 vs ref 122.56) and Gilts (86.50 vs ref 86.24) are close to current levels. The OAT cover level is 111.40 vs ref 110.06.
Japan rates: CTAs are moderately long JGBs and add to longs above 127.14 (JBZ6 ref 126.85).
Oil: CTAs were signaled to trim their longs after the post-election selloff continued through the first trigger. The level to flip short WTI is 80.85 (CLZ6 ref 87.28), 7.4% below current levels.
Precious metals: CTAs are 'max short' gold and silver. First cover levels are 4284 in gold (+5.7% vs 4053 GCZ6) and 61.41 in silver (+16.3% vs 52.80 SIZ6).

FX: CTAs are 'max long' USD across all six pairs as USD outperformed following the election. The nearest levels where they start reducing USD longs are GBPUSD 134.00 (BPZ6 ref 133.12) and USDJPY 63.48 (JYZ6 ref 63.00). EURUSD (1.1422 vs ref 1.1151) and USDCAD (71.61 vs ref 70.36) are further away.

Citi's CTA model has four regimes: 'max' short, moderately short, moderately long and 'max' long. A 'max' regime does not mean positioning has reached a historical max. The estimates are proprietary and may not match actual CTA positioning or returns.
risk_factors: A reversal in the SX5E rally below 6313 would halt CTA buying in European equities.
A rally of about 1% in US equity indices would trigger CTA buying or short covering in SPX, NDX and RTY.
A Treasury reversal to 106-11 in TY would signal CTA buying, ending the current selling pressure.
Further oil weakness to 80.85 in CLZ6 would flip CTAs from long to short WTI.
vol_and_positioning: CTAs are short to 'max short' in US equities (NDX and RTY 'max short', SPX moderately short) and 'max short' in TU, FV and TY Treasury futures.
CTAs are 'max long' USD across all six FX pairs tracked and 'max short' gold and silver.
CTAs are long Europe equities (SX5E) and moderately long JGBs, while 'max short' EM (MXEF) and Japan (NKY) equities.
Short-covering triggers in US equity indices sit within 1% of current levels, so a modest rally would flip or reduce CTA shorts in SPX, NDX and RTY.
CTAs are being signaled to trim oil longs, with the flip-short level 7.4% below spot at 80.85 in CLZ6.
geopolitical: US midterm election results are cited as the driver of the USD outperformance and the oil reversal in the CTA signals.
